title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 650 bis–787, continuing La Longue Marche). Grothendieck is studying group schemes over a base S over S_0 that model profinite groups. These are abelianised fundamental groups of a torus-type or once-punctured genus-1 situation, together with the cyclotomic or Galois action on them.

The objects are as follows.
- M ≅ (Π_0)^ab ≅ Z^2. Its profinite version is M^.
- H^+ = S^+/M is a discrete group, and H^+/F ≅ S_3 (plausibly GL_2(F_2)).
- On the previous page Grothendieck proved that the extension S^+ of H^+ by M splits over any base S. Two splittings are conjugate by a unique section of M.
- G_{ρ,σ} is an extension of Φ_12^* × H^+ by M. Here Φ_12^* is the group-scheme avatar of Ẑ^* (cyclotomic units) and μ_C = {1,ω} is a constant Z/2 over S_0. The element ω is a central sign, morally −1.

On this page he takes a section subgroup H(ρ',σ') ⊂ G_{ρ,σ} lying over H^+. It is generated by lifts ρ', σ' of the generators ρ, σ. He computes its centraliser in four steps.
1. A priori the centraliser lies in Φ_12^*·(M × μ_C). Its elements are written λ ω^i u_μ, with λ ∈ ΓM, μ ∈ ΓΦ_12^* and i ∈ Γ(Z/2)_{S_0}.
2. Since ω is central, λω^i u_μ centralises iff λ u_μ does. So only the pair (λ, μ) matters.
3. Commuting with ρ' gives the same condition (260) as before, with no change.
4. Commuting with σ' is where the new point lies. In the earlier computation (p. 703') one used ω^{ν_2} = 1, which is no longer allowed. The condition becomes ω^{ν_2(μ)} λ η^{μ} σ(λ^{-1}) = η. Because ω is a non-trivial sign independent of the M-part, this splits into two conditions:
   - (270) ν_2(μ) = 0, i.e. μ lies in the index-2 subgroup Φ_12^{*''};
   - relation (261) on λ.

Under ν_2(μ) = 0 the earlier calculations (pp. 703'–704) apply verbatim.

The corollary is started here and finished on the next page. For every lift T of S^+ over H^+, the centraliser T sits in an exact sequence 1 → M^(…) → T → Φ_12^{*''} → 1, and T^♮ ≅ Φ_12^{*''}. This gives two consequences.
- The extension G_{ρ,σ} of Φ_12^* × H^+ by M splits over no non-empty S. Profinitely: G_{ρ,σ} of Ẑ^* × H^+ by M^ is non-split.
- The restriction G'' to the index-2 subgroup Φ_12^{*''} × H^+ (resp. Ẑ^{*''} × H^+) does split. Its splittings form a torsor under M (resp. M^) and correspond bijectively, by restriction, to splittings of S^+ (B^) over H^+.

In short: a parity character ν_2 on the cyclotomic group is the exact obstruction to splitting the arithmetic extension compatibly with the geometric symmetry group H^+.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The step 'condition ⇔ (ν_2(μ)=0 and (261))' needs ω to be independent of the M-part, i.e. ω ∉ M and the product M × μ_C is direct. The page assumes this without restating it.
The transcription garbles several words (see corrections), making the logic of the commutation-with-ρ' sentence unclear. The intended meaning is that (260) applies unchanged.

ideas.what: Computing the centraliser of a lifted finite symmetry subgroup inside an extension of (cyclotomic group × finite group) by Z^2, in order to decide splitting.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting / section analysis of an arithmetic fundamental group extension, centraliser of a lifted finite group (Galois-equivariant lifts of torsion symmetries)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, Ihara, Matsumoto et al. for the Galois action on π1 of genus-1 curves; the general method is folklore
ideas.where_published: Only in the archive notes (La Longue Marche, suite).

ideas.what: A sign/parity character ν_2 on Ẑ^* (Φ_12^*) obstructs splitting; on its kernel (index 2) the extension splits, with splittings a torsor under M^ (conjugation).
ideas.modern_name: Index-2 (sign) obstruction to splitting the Galois action on the abelianised π1 of a genus-1 curve with automorphisms; ±1 ambiguity of the cyclotomic lift
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unsure; similar ±1 phenomena appear in work on Galois actions on Teichmüller groupoids / GT
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as I know.

ideas.what: Group-scheme ('sur une base S quelconque') formulation of discrete/profinite splitting statements, deducing the profinite statement from the scheme-theoretic one.
ideas.modern_name: Constant/twisted group schemes modelling profinite Galois data

missed.claim: An explicit theorem with a precise obstruction. The extension of Ẑ^* × H^+ by M^ ≅ Ẑ^2 is not split. Its restriction to the index-2 subgroup ker ν_2 splits, with splittings an M^-torsor in bijection with splittings of B^ over H^+. The obstruction is a parity character ν_2. This is a concrete, finished computation in the arithmetic of π1 in genus 1 that does not appear (credited to Grothendieck) in the literature, though it may be equivalent to known facts about the ±1 issue.
missed.quote: ne pas plus écrire ω^{ν_2}=1, la condition s'écrit ω^{ν_2}λη^uσ(λ^{-1})=η ... (270) ν_2(μ)=0 i.e. μ∈ΓΦ_12^{*''}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on Galois-equivariant lifts of finite symmetry groups in genus-1 Teichmüller towers and on the GT-action on M_{1,1}/M_{1,2} data, where sign/2-adic subtleties are known to be delicate. It may be a minor, likely re-derivable fact.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, essentially routine centraliser computation within a long technical development. The non-splitting by a parity character is a nice precise statement, but probably equivalent to known ±1 phenomena and not striking on its own.
transcription_corrections: 'sous-groupe certain' should read 'sous-groupe section' (also in the corollary: 'des sous-groupes sections H(ρ',σ')').
'sans changement ni variation' / 'Pour le calcul p. 703 i.e. quant à une variation' is garbled; the sense is that (260) applies with no change, as in the calculation p. 703.
'la calcul de p. 703' doit se modifier en ne pas plus écrire ω^{ν_2}=1' should read 'le calcul de p. 703' doit se modifier en ce qu'on ne peut plus écrire ω^{ν_2}=1'.
'et équivaut : la conjonction' should read 'et équivaut à la conjonction'.
'En prenant de ν_2(μ)=0' should read 'En partant de ν_2(μ)=0' (or 'En tenant compte de').
's'appliquent, finalement on trouve' should read 's'appliquant, finalement on trouve'.

In the corollary, the struck word is 'centralisateur'; the insertion reads 'tout relevé T de S^+ au-dessus de H^+'. The last line likely reads 'le centralisateur dans G_{ρ,σ} des sous-groupes sections H(ρ',σ') est …'.
